Create a fictional educational explainer for CYBERAWARE 3D about Insider threat. Scenario: A staff member with legitimate access downloads an unusually large volume of project files outside their normal work pattern. There is no evidence yet of data exfiltration or malicious intent. Explain why the correct defensive response is: Preserve relevant authorized telemetry and route the observable anomaly to the designated security/insider-risk process for proportionate review. Also contrast the unsafe alternatives using short abstract visual cues. Conclude with: An indicator is a reason for proportionate review—not a diagnosis of motive or guilt. Use a generic simulated interface, a navy/cyan 3D cyber-learning environment, legible labels, restrained camera motion, no recognizable logos, no real personal data, no operational attack instructions, no real credentials or live URLs.

VISUAL STYLE
Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

GENERATION INSTRUCTIONS
- Use the narration as the voiceover source; preserve its meaning and do not add unsupported technical claims.
- Render a 16:9 MP4 at 1080p or equivalent; keep text inside safe margins.
- Use only fictional names, domains, screens and values. Never render real secrets, OTPs, account data or real target systems.
- Provide a separate WebVTT caption file and transcript; do not rely on burned-in text alone.
- Use no flashing effects, rapid strobing, unnecessary parallax or autoplay audio.
- Human-review the rendered video for factual accuracy, spelling, pronunciation, captions and timing before marking it validated.
